pll2d16c3-d1e3519.summary: States that image and likeness here can be taken as uncreated, the Trinity's essence to which man was made, or as created, in which man was made, concreated with him.
claims: Image may be uncreated or created.

pll2d16c3-d1e3522.summary: Notes that Bede seems to mean the uncreated image when he says the image is of the three persons, not of God and angels; but this is improperly called image, since image is relative to that whose likeness it bears and represents, as Caesar's image; that to which something is made is improperly an image, as exemplar differs from example. The Son is properly the Father's image.
claims: The Trinity's essence is improperly called image.
The Son is properly the Father's image.

pll2d16c3-d1e3540.summary: Reports some who took 'image' here as the Son and said man is not the image but made to the image.

pll2d16c3-d1e3544.summary: Refutes them with 1 Cor 11:7, 'man is the image and glory of God,' and the word 'our': if the image were the Son alone, it would not say 'our,' since the Son is the Father's image only.
claims: Man is the image of God.
'Our image' cannot mean the Son alone.

pll2d16c3-d1e3565.summary: Reports others, more perceptive, who took the image as the Son and the likeness as the Spirit, the likeness of Father and Son; they referred 'our' to likeness only and held man to be image and made to the image and likeness, image of image and likeness.
claims: One view: image is the Son, likeness the Spirit.

pll2d16c3-d1e3576.summary: Judges this not wholly reprehensible but lacking the saints' authority; more fittingly the image and likeness are sought in man himself: made to God's image and likeness by the mind, by which he surpasses irrational beings; to the image in memory, understanding, and love; to the likeness in innocence and justice, natural to the rational mind.
claims: Image is in memory, understanding, and love.
Likeness is in innocence and justice.

pll2d16c3-d1e3588.summary: Offers alternatives: image in knowledge of truth, likeness in love of virtue or truth; or image in everything else, likeness in essence, since the soul is immortal and indivisible.
claims: Other readings of image and likeness.

pll2d16c3-d1e3591.summary: Cites Augustine: the soul was made like God because he made it immortal and indissoluble; image pertains to form, likeness to nature. So man by the soul is made to the image of the whole Trinity, not one person, and is called image because God's image is in him, as a panel is called a picture because of the painting.
claims: Likeness pertains to the soul's immortality.
Man is made to the image of the whole Trinity.
Man is called image because the image is in him.

pl-l2d16c3.summary: Explains the image and likeness. They can be taken as uncreated, the essence of the Trinity to which man was made (Bede), though this is improperly called 'image,' since image is properly relative, as the Son is properly the Father's image; or as created, concreated with man. Some held the image here is the Son and man only 'to' the image, but Paul calls man the image of God (1 Cor 11:7), and 'our' excludes the Son alone. Others took image as the Son and likeness as the Spirit, which is not wholly blameworthy but lacks the authority of the saints. More fittingly, the image and likeness are in man's mind: image in memory, understanding, and love; likeness in innocence and justice; or image in knowledge of truth and likeness in love of virtue; or likeness in the soul's immortality and indivisibility (Augustine). So man is made, by the soul, to the image of the whole Trinity, and is called image because the image is in him, as a panel is called a picture.
claims: Image and likeness can mean the uncreated Trinity or a created image in man.
'Image' properly means something relative, as the Son is the Father's image.
Man is the image of God, not only made to the image (1 Cor 11:7).
Reading image as Son and likeness as Spirit lacks authority.
Image lies in memory, understanding, and love; likeness in innocence and justice.
Alternatively, likeness lies in the soul's immortality and indivisibility.
Man is the image of the whole Trinity by his soul.
